subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Why Every Culture Needs One
description: A fast breakdown of Why Every Culture Needs One for builders.

hook.text: Tricksters appear on every continent. No mythology lacks one. Their universality demands explanation.

buildup.text: Cultures need a figure who tests limits. Laws only have meaning when someone dares to break them.

discovery.text: Anthropologist Paul Radin argued the trickster is the oldest mythic figure—older than gods or heroes.

twist.text: The trickster may be the first story we told ourselves: someone who breaks the rules and survives.

climax.text: Order alone is sterile. Chaos alone is destruction. The trickster dances between them and makes culture.

punchline.text: Without a rule-breaker, rules mean nothing.

quiz.question: Who argued the trickster is the oldest mythic figure?
